instruction:
Repo: Go project at /gin (gin web framework). Use ONLY files in /gin (no internet, no other copies of gin). Another subagent may be editing /gin/gin.go concurrently — do NOT touch gin.go.

BUG (panic "invalid node type" in case-insensitive path lookup): With `RedirectFixedPath = true` and routes `r.GET("/prefix/:id", h)` and `r.GET("/prefix/xxx", h)`, requesting `/PREFIX/XXX` or `/prefix/a/b/c` panics with `panic: invalid node type` instead of redirecting (or 404ing). Cause: in /gin/tree.go, `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` does, after the `if !n.wildChild { ... }` block:

    n = n.children[0]
    switch n.nType {
    case param: ...
    case catchAll: ...
    default:
        panic("invalid node type")
    }

But the repo's own invariant (see the comment "Handle wildcard child, which is always at the end of the array" in `node.getValue`, and how `addRoute` appends the wildcard child) is that the wildcard child is the LAST child. When the node also has static children (e.g. "xxx" before ":id"), `children[0]` is a static node whose nType falls into `default` -> panic. Also check the other `n = n.children[0]` inside the `case param:` branch of the same function and fix it the same way if it is the wildcard-child access (verify by reading the code; do not change unrelated logic).

FIX: use the last child, i.e. `n = n.children[len(n.children)-1]`, in the place(s) where the wildcard child is meant. Keep the existing `panic("invalid node type")` default branch (the pre-existing test TestTreeInvalidNodeType relies on it: it sets children[0].nType = 42 on a node with a single wildcard child and expects a panic from findCaseInsensitivePath — with one child, last == first, so it still panics). Do NOT edit any pre-existing *_test.go file. Do not reformat unrelated code.

VERIFICATION (run all of it yourself with bash):
1. Baseline: `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`; record results.
2. Apply the fix (re-read /gin/tree.go right before editing since another agent may have touched it; if it was modified, only change the wildcard-child access lines).
3. Rerun `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`; every baseline-passing test must still pass. Report output.
4. Temporary test /gin/zz_tmp_fixedpath_test.go (package gin) — run `cd /gin && go test -run TestTmpFixedPathPanic -v . 2>&1 | tail -30`:

package gin

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"
)

func TestTmpFixedPathPanic(t *testing.T) {
	r := New()
	r.RedirectFixedPath = true
	r.GET("/prefix/:id", func(c *Context) { c.String(200, "param") })
	r.GET("/prefix/xxx", func(c *Context) { c.String(200, "static") })

	for _, p := range []string{"/PREFIX/XXX", "/prefix/a/b/c", "/prefix/xxx", "/prefix/123"} {
		w := httptest.NewRecorder()
		req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, p, nil)
		defer func() {
			if rec := recover(); rec != nil {
				t.Fatalf("panic for %s: %v", p, rec)
			}
		}()
		r.ServeHTTP(w, req)
		t.Logf("%s -> %d %q", p, w.Code, w.Header().Get("Location"))
	}
}

Confirm it PANICS before the fix and does not after (revert/apply as needed). Then delete the temp file and check `git -C /gin status --porcelain` shows only intended source files (errors.go, response_writer.go, gin.go may already be modified by other work — leave them alone).

REPORT: exact diff of tree.go, baseline vs after test output, temp test output before/after, git status.

Repo: Go project at /gin (gin web framework). Use ONLY files in /gin (no internet, no other copies).

BUG (runtime route registration loses URL params): If a route with params is registered AFTER the engine has already served a request, a subsequent matching request returns 200 but all params are empty (`c.Param("name") == ""`, `c.Params.ByName("last_name") == ""`, `c.Params.Get("wild")` returns "",false). Repro: create `r := gin.New()`, do `PerformRequest(r, "GET", "/test/john/smith/is/super/great")` (404), then `r.GET("/test/:name/:last_name/*wild", handler)`, then repeat the same request -> 200 but params empty. Params must be populated exactly as when the route is registered before the first request.

Likely cause: `Engine.maxParams`/`maxSections` are only used when a Context is created (`allocateContext` / sync.Pool New), and pooled contexts created before the route existed have `cap(*params) == 0`; `node.getValue` only saves params when `params != nil && cap(*params) > 0`. Investigate gin.go (allocateContext, addRoute, handleHTTPRequest, pool) and tree.go (getValue param saving). Implement a MINIMAL fix so params work for routes added at runtime, e.g. by making the context allocation use the current maxParams (re-allocate/reuse a context whose params capacity is too small) — do not change unrelated behavior and do not edit any pre-existing *_test.go file.

VERIFICATION (run everything yourself):
1. Baseline `cd /gin && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -40`; record pass/fail.
2. Apply fix; rerun full suite; every baseline-passing test must still pass. Report output.
3. Add a TEMPORARY test file /gin/zz_tmp_runtime_route_test.go (package gin) that does exactly the repro above plus the same check with the route registered before any request, and run `cd /gin && go test -run TestTmpRuntimeRoute -v . 2>&1 | tail -20`. Confirm it FAILS before the fix and PASSES after (revert/apply as needed).
4. Delete the temp file; `git -C /gin status --porcelain` must show only your intended source file(s) modified (errors.go and response_writer.go are already modified by other work — leave them alone).

REPORT: exact diff, baseline vs after test output, temp test output before/after fix, git status.
